result.instructions: Tools for choosing audio from an indexed library. Describe what you want with `search_music` (it needs a model), pick one result, `set_anchor` it, then ask `find_compatible_music` or `find_compatible_sfx` for what belongs beside it and `explain_match` for why something ranked where it did. An `asset_id` is the 16-character content hash a result returned, never a path. The anchor belongs to this connection and is lost when it closes. `k` is a bound from 1 to 100, not a page: ask for a larger `k` to see more.

tools.description: Find audio in the library by describing it in words, best match first. Returns at most `k` results, each with its score, why it scored that way, and where the asset came from. It does not use the session's anchor: pass `anchor` to judge every result against that asset's loudness, tempo and key. search_music: safe to retry. The same arguments give the same answer field for field, so a retry after a timeout is a second read rather than a second effect.

anchor.description: An asset to judge results against, as 16 lowercase hex characters. Omit to rank by the description alone.

description.description: What you want to hear, in words: for example `tense, sparse strings, underwater ruins`.

k.description: How many results at most. A bound, not a page: ask for a larger `k` to see more.

tools.name: search_music

tools.description: Choose the asset the next questions are about, and learn what the library knows about it: loudness, spectrum, tempo, key and where it came from. `find_compatible_music` and `find_compatible_sfx` use it when you pass no `anchor`. It belongs to this connection and is lost when the connection closes. set_anchor: safe to retry. The same arguments give the same answer field for field, so a retry after a timeout is a second read rather than a second effect.

asset_id.description: The asset: 16 lowercase hex characters, exactly as an earlier result returned it.

tools.name: set_anchor

tools.description: Find music that fits the anchor, best first: similar in sound and compatible in loudness, tempo and key. It reports what it excluded and why, so a short list is explained. Uses the anchor `set_anchor` chose unless you pass one. find_compatible_music: safe to retry. The same arguments give the same answer field for field, so a retry after a timeout is a second read rather than a second effect.

anchor.description: The asset to fit, as 16 lowercase hex characters. Omit to use the anchor `set_anchor` chose.

k.description: How many results at most. A bound, not a page: ask for a larger `k` to see more.

tools.name: find_compatible_music

tools.description: Find sound effects that belong in the same world as the anchor, best first. Near-identical variants of one sound are reported, not returned a dozen times. Uses the anchor `set_anchor` chose unless you pass one. find_compatible_sfx: safe to retry. The same arguments give the same answer field for field, so a retry after a timeout is a second read rather than a second effect.

anchor.description: The asset to fit, as 16 lowercase hex characters. Omit to use the anchor `set_anchor` chose.

category.description: Keep only assets whose recorded source contains this text, case-insensitively: for example `footsteps`.

k.description: How many results at most. A bound, not a page: ask for a larger `k` to see more.

tools.name: find_compatible_sfx

tools.description: Explain why `asset_id` scores what it does against `anchor`: every signal's raw value, weight and contribution, and a sentence naming what carried it and what counted against it. Use it when a ranking looks wrong. explain_match: safe to retry. The same arguments give the same answer field for field, so a retry after a timeout is a second read rather than a second effect.

anchor.description: The asset it is compared against, as 16 lowercase hex characters.

asset_id.description: The asset: 16 lowercase hex characters, exactly as an earlier result returned it.

tools.name: explain_match

tools.description: Play an asset through the game's own audio so a person can hear it. It needs a running app, and this server has none, so it answers `unavailable`. audition: NOT safe to retry. It starts a voice, so a retry plays the sound twice and can itself produce a VoiceLimit refusal that the first call did not.

asset_id.description: The asset: 16 lowercase hex characters, exactly as an earlier result returned it.

bus.description: The bus to play on. `Effects` when omitted.

tools.name: audition
